fields.distribution: Primary strike fly in Europe and North America
fields.significance: Maggots cause strike in sheep and wound myiasis in dogs and cats; severe cases can be fatal if untreated.

lifecycleStages.name: egg
lifecycleStages.location: laid on fouled fleece or wounds of the live animal; hatch within about a day in moist conditions

lifecycleStages.name: larva
lifecycleStages.location: maggots crawl over and into the wound or skin lesion, often at the breech of sheep, until mature and then leave the lesion

lifecycleStages.name: pupa
lifecycleStages.location: fully grown maggots fall off and form puparia in the soil

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: free-living fly attracted to wounds, soiled coats and decaying matter

fields.distribution: Cattle in the northern hemisphere
fields.significance: Larvae under the skin of the back perforate the hide, and egg-laying flies panic cattle, cutting weight gain and milk yield.

lifecycleStages.name: egg
lifecycleStages.location: stuck one at a time to hairs over the rump and top of the hind leg in summer

lifecycleStages.name: L1
lifecycleStages.location: hatch in under a week, burrow through the skin and travel inside the body, overwintering in the epidural fat after following the nerves

lifecycleStages.name: L2
lifecycleStages.location: arrive under the skin of the back in late winter and develop there

lifecycleStages.name: L3
lifecycleStages.location: lie in a swelling on the back with a breathing hole in the skin, then emerge in spring and drop to the ground

lifecycleStages.name: pupa
lifecycleStages.location: form puparia on the ground after falling from the back

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: free-living; mouthparts are vestigial so the fly does not feed, and it mates and dies within a couple of weeks

fields.significance: Larvae irritate the nose and sinus, giving discharge and sneezing; attacking flies stress the flock, and rare heavy infections reach the brain.

lifecycleStages.location: nasal passages, where larvae may stay dormant through the winter

lifecycleStages.name: L3
lifecycleStages.location: frontal sinus, then returns to the nostrils and is sneezed out onto the ground

lifecycleStages.name: pupa
lifecycleStages.location: pupates in the environment

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: free-living; females live only about two weeks

fields.distribution: Horses and other equids worldwide
fields.significance: Larvae in the stomach can erode the mucosa, though signs are rare; egg-laying adult flies distress horses.

lifecycleStages.name: egg
lifecycleStages.location: attached to hairs, mainly of the forelimbs and shoulders; the larva develops in the egg in about ten days and hatches when the horse licks or bites

lifecycleStages.name: L1
lifecycleStages.location: hatches from the egg, gets into the mouth and burrows about in the tongue, with the gums also visited at times, for around four weeks

lifecycleStages.name: L2
lifecycleStages.location: swallowed, then fixed to the lining of the stomach near the cardia

lifecycleStages.name: L3
lifecycleStages.location: stays fixed in the stomach for several months, then lets go and leaves in the faeces

lifecycleStages.name: pupa
lifecycleStages.location: pupates in the environment after passing out in the faeces

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: free-living; lacks functional mouthparts and does not feed, and lives only a few days

lifecycleStages.location: deposited after a blood meal, in wet soil by water or in decaying plant matter

lifecycleStages.name: larva
lifecycleStages.location: four instars, living in that same wet soil or decaying plant matter

lifecycleStages.name: pupa
lifecycleStages.location: pupates there; pupae in water float to the surface before the adult emerges

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: females bite and blood-feed every few days, mainly around dusk, night and dawn

lifecycleStages.name: larva

lifecycleStages.name: pupa
lifecycleStages.location: pupates in the environment

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: both sexes blood-feed on the host, most actively around sunrise and sunset, and then leave it

lifecycleStages.name: larva

lifecycleStages.location: pupates in a cocoon in the dung

lifecycleStages.name: adult
lifecycleStages.location: moves over the face and eyes, taking up eye and nose secretions and blood from wounds opened by other flies; leaves the host only briefly to lay eggs
